links.reason: Romans repeats Isaiah: without those the Lord of Hosts left, “we would have become like Sodom, we would have resembled Gomorrah”.
Revelation repeats the cry “Holy, Holy, Holy” from Isaiah, but names “the Lord God Almighty” where Isaiah names “the LORD of Hosts”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “ever hearing but never understanding” and “ever seeing but never perceiving”.
Mark repeats Isaiah: “ever seeing but never perceiving” and “ever hearing but never understanding”.
Acts repeats Isaiah: “ever hearing but never understanding” and “ever seeing but never perceiving”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts”.
John repeats Isaiah: “understand with their hearts, and turn”, then “I would heal them” where Isaiah says “be healed”.
Acts repeats Isaiah: “see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “the virgin will be with child”, “give birth to a son”, and “call Him Immanuel”.
1 Peter repeats Isaiah: “Do not fear what they fear”, then “do not be shaken” where Isaiah says “do not live in dread”.
Romans repeats Isaiah: “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense”.
1 Peter repeats Isaiah: “a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense”.
Hebrews repeats Isaiah: “I will put My trust in Him”; in Isaiah, the speaker also says “I will wait for the LORD”.
Hebrews repeats Isaiah: “Here am I, and the children”, then “God has given Me” where Isaiah says “the LORD has given me”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “the Way of the Sea, beyond the Jordan”, naming the land of Zebulun and Naphtali, and “Galilee of the Gentiles”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: people in darkness “have seen a great light”, and for those in “the shadow of death, a light has dawned”.
Romans repeats Isaiah: “like the sand of the sea”, then “only the remnant will be saved” where Isaiah has “only a remnant will return”.
Romans says “the Lord will carry out His sentence on the earth”; Isaiah says “will carry out the destruction decreed”.
2 Thessalonians repeats Isaiah: the Lord Jesus will “slay with the breath of His mouth”, where Isaiah says “breath of His lips”.
Romans repeats Isaiah: “the Root of Jesse”, and says the Gentiles put their hope in Him, while Isaiah says “The nations will seek Him”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “you will be brought down to” Hades, where Isaiah has Sheol.
Luke repeats Isaiah: “you will be brought down to” Hades, where Isaiah has Sheol.
1 Corinthians repeats Isaiah: “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die”.
Revelation repeats Isaiah: “What He opens no one can shut”, and speaks of “the key of David”.
1 Corinthians has “foreign lips I will speak to this people”; Isaiah has “foreign tongues, He will speak to this people”.
Romans repeats Isaiah: “the one who believes”, with “will never be put to shame” where Isaiah says “will never be shaken”.
Romans says “Anyone who believes in Him will never be put to shame”; Isaiah says “the one who believes will never be shaken”.
1 Peter repeats “precious cornerstone” and “the one who believes” from Isaiah, which has “See, I lay a stone in Zion”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me”.
Mark repeats Isaiah: “honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me”.
Mark says “they teach as doctrine the precepts of men”; Isaiah says “Their worship of Me is but rules taught by men”.
1 Corinthians repeats Isaiah: “the wisdom of the wise” and “the intelligence of the intelligent”, with “I will destroy” where Isaiah says “will vanish”.
Romans repeats the question in Isaiah: “Shall what is formed say to Him who formed it”.
Hebrews says “strengthen your limp hands and weak knees”; Isaiah says “Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “A voice of one calling” and “Prepare the way for the Lord”; Matthew places “in the wilderness” after the voice.
Luke repeats Isaiah: “A voice of one calling” and “Prepare the way for the Lord”; Luke places “in the wilderness” after the voice.
John repeats Isaiah: “voice of one calling”; John has “Make straight the way for the Lord”, Isaiah has “Prepare the way for the LORD”.
Luke repeats Isaiah: “every mountain and hill made low”; Luke says the valley is “filled in” where Isaiah says “lifted up”.
Luke has “all humanity will see God’s salvation”; Isaiah has “all humanity together will see it”.
1 Peter repeats Isaiah: “All flesh is like grass” and “all its glory like the flowers of the field”.
1 Peter repeats Isaiah: “the grass withers and the flowers fall”.
1 Peter says “the word of the Lord stands forever”; Isaiah says “the word of our God stands forever”.
Romans asks who has known “the mind of the Lord” and been “His counselor”; Isaiah asks who has directed “the Spirit of the LORD”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah: “Here is My Servant”, “in whom My soul delights”, and “I will put My Spirit on Him”.
Matthew repeats Isaiah’s words about one who will not cry out, whose voice is not heard “in the streets.”
Matthew repeats Isaiah’s words: “A bruised reed He will not break,” and a smoldering wick He will not put out.
Matthew and Isaiah both say people “will put their hope”: in “His name” in Matthew, and in “His law” in Isaiah.
Romans repeats Isaiah’s picture of every knee that “will bow before Me,” with every tongue speaking to God.
Philippians repeats Isaiah’s words that every knee will bow and every tongue speak, now at “the name of Jesus.”
Acts repeats Isaiah’s words about a “light” to bring salvation “to the ends of the earth,” naming the Gentiles where Isaiah has the nations.
2 Corinthians repeats Isaiah’s promise of help in “the time of favor” and “the day of salvation,” then says that time is now.
Romans says “God’s name is blasphemed among the Gentiles”; Isaiah has the LORD say “My name is blasphemed continually all day long.”
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words about messengers: “How beautiful” are “the feet of those who bring good news.”
2 Corinthians repeats Isaiah’s command “Touch no unclean thing,” and both passages call people to come out.
Romans says those not told about Him “will see”; Isaiah says kings “will see what they have not been told.”
John repeats Isaiah’s questions “Who has believed our message?” and “to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?”
Romans repeats Isaiah’s question about who “has believed our message,” after saying not all welcomed the good news.
Matthew repeats Isaiah’s words “took up our infirmities and carried our” burdens; Matthew ends with “diseases,” Isaiah with “sorrows.”
1 Peter repeats Isaiah’s words that by “His stripes” people “are healed,” saying you where Isaiah says we.
Acts repeats Isaiah’s words about one led “to the slaughter” who “did not open His mouth,” like a silent lamb or sheep.
Acts repeats Isaiah’s question about who “can recount His descendants,” and says His life was removed from the earth.
1 Peter repeats Isaiah’s words that no “deceit” was in “His mouth,” and adds that He committed no sin.
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words “He was numbered with the transgressors” as something that must happen “in Me.”
Hebrews says Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many; Isaiah says “He bore the sin of many.”
Galatians repeats Isaiah’s call to “O barren woman, who bears no children,” and to break forth and cry aloud.
John repeats Isaiah’s words that people “will be taught by” God; Isaiah says it of “all your sons.”
Acts has “I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David”; Isaiah has an everlasting covenant, “My loving devotion promised to David.”
Matthew repeats Isaiah’s words “My house will be called a house of prayer.”
Mark repeats Isaiah’s words “My house will be called a house of prayer” and “for all the nations.”
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words about “a house of prayer,” but leaves out “called” and “for all the nations.”
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words about people whose feet are “swift to shed” blood.
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words “lie in their wake,” saying ruin and misery where Isaiah says ruin and destruction.
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words “the way of peace they have not known.”
Ephesians says “take the helmet of salvation”; Isaiah says He put on “the helmet of salvation on His head.”
Romans says “The Deliverer will come from Zion”; Isaiah says “The Redeemer will come to Zion,” with “Jacob” in both.
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words “this is My covenant with them” and adds that God takes away their sins.
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words “to preach good news to the poor” and “to proclaim liberty to the captives.”
Luke repeats Isaiah’s words about proclaiming “the year of the” Lord’s favor; Isaiah then adds “the day of our God’s vengeance.”
Matthew says “your King comes to you”; Isaiah says “your Savior comes,” in the same call to say to the Daughter of Zion.
1 Corinthians repeats “no eye has seen” from Isaiah, and both passages speak of God acting for those who love or wait for Him.
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words “I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me,” and the line about being found.
Romans repeats Isaiah’s words “All day long I have held out My hands to” an obstinate people, adding “disobedient.”
2 Peter looks forward to “a new heaven and a new earth”; Isaiah says “I will create new heavens and a new earth.”
Acts repeats Isaiah’s words “Heaven is My throne” and “What kind of house will you build for Me?”
Acts repeats Isaiah’s question “Has not My hand made all these things?”
Mark repeats Isaiah’s words about “their worm” that never dies and a fire never “quenched.”
Mark repeats Isaiah’s words “A voice of one calling” and “Prepare the way for the” Lord, with the voice in the wilderness.
Romans strings together sayings and includes “Their feet are swift to shed blood”; Isaiah says “they are swift to shed innocent blood.”
Revelation has “I am the First and the Last”; Isaiah has the LORD say “the first and the last.”
Revelation has “I am the First and the Last”; Isaiah has the LORD say “I am the first and I am the last.”
Revelation repeats Isaiah’s promise that people will not hunger or thirst, and that no “scorching heat” or sun will beat down on them.
